title: Records with Clarence Williams and King Oliver; the Oliver band in New York
summary: She made records for Columbia with Clarence Williams, probably with King Oliver on cornet. She describes Oliver's band struggling in New York and Louis Russell taking it over.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Yeah, he was. Then I Made On The Columbia with Clarence Williams. And I think on a couple of those records, he used... Now, maybe that was King Oliver, that cornet, because I did make a record.
My different kind of man and you're such a cruel papa.
That was with Clarence Williams. That's right. That was with Clarence Williams. That's his number.
And I believe that had a cornet on it.
Well, that's it. Because I think those were the ones I made with King Oliver. Yeah. Yeah.
And you remember anybody else in the band? Have a clarinet player?
Joe was having a hard time then, huh?

Well, those New York musicians, they was against those Western boys coming in there. That's the guys coming from Chicago, you know? It seemed to give them a hard way to go, you know? And I think that's where his band broke up from him there, you know? I think Russell, this Louis Russell, I think, then took the band over or something. The piano player. Hmm? But then I went, I went, then he started, he was getting jobs like in Atlantic City, you know? I went with him twice to Atlantic City. He's in Ryan. On, yeah, on a couple jobs. We drove there by car, you know?
Did he have any other New Orleans musicians with him? Anybody else remember being outstanding?
From New Orleans? Yeah. I think he did. I think he did. I think Albert Nichols was with him.
Well, that's that Louis Russell bunch, aren't we?

That's King Oliver's bunch, you see? They double-crossed King, and that's where Russell got the bunch. Something came up there, and that's where I think they all swung with Russell. That's the whole bunch that was with King when he came there to New York. Pops Foster? Well, I don't exactly remember, you know, who they were.
